The '''2018–19 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team'''  represented the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team's [[head coach]] was [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]], who was in his 16th season as UNC's head men's basketball coach. The Tar Heels played their home games at the [[Dean Smith Center]] in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They finished the season 29–7, 16–2 in ACC play to finish tied for the regular season conference championship with [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2019 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they advanced to the semifinals before ultimately losing to [[2018–19 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the Midwest region, where they advanced to the Sweet Sixteen before losing to [[2018–19 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]].

==Previous season==

The [[2017–18 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|Tar Heels]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] with a record of 26–11, 11–7 in [[2017-18 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a four-way tie for third place. As the No. 6 seed in the [[2018 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401019991|title=Syracuse vs. North Carolina – Game Recap – March 7, 2018 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-04-05}}</ref> [[2017–18 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/unc-tops-miami-acc-tournament-sets-rematch-duke-article-1.3864396|title=UNC tops Miami in ACC tournament, sets up rematch with Duke|work=NY Daily News|access-date=2018-04-05|language=en}}</ref> and [[2017–18 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/10/north-carolina-holds-off-duke-acc-semifinals/413035002/|title=No. 11 North Carolina holds off No. 4 Duke in ACC semifinals|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2018-04-05|language=en}}</ref> before losing to [[2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the championship game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/10/sports/virginia-defeats-north-carolina-for-acc-championship.html|title=Virginia Defeats North Carolina for A.C.C. Championship|last=Tracy|first=Marc|date=2018-03-10|work=The New York Times|access-date=2018-04-05|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the West region where they defeated [[2017–18 Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball team|Lipscomb]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025839|title=Lipscomb vs. North Carolina – Game Recap – March 16, 2018 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-04-05}}</ref> before losing to [[2017–18 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the second round.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2018/03/18/texas-am-north-carolina-ncaa-tournament/|title=March Madness: No. 7 Texas A&M stuns No. 2 North Carolina in NCAA Tournament|date=2018-03-18|work=The Denver Post|access-date=2018-04-05|language=en-US}}</ref>
